headline: Last session: Indian markets snapped two-week gains as surging crude oil prices above $114 weighed on sentiment.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 26 October.

why: Surging crude oil prices nearing $114 per barrel pressured Indian equities.
The Sensex shed over 1,600 points across a turbulent trading week.
Snapping a two-week winning streak, major indices ended lower due to extended selling pressure.
Rising commodity costs impacted profitability outlooks for key manufacturing segments.
whatHappening: Nifty closed around 22,600 as indices ended the week on a weak note.
Coforge raised its FY27 margin guidance as AI alters its cost structure.
U.S. FDA issued four observations to Gland Pharma's Hyderabad formulation facility.
Kilitch Drugs announced an agreement to divest its Ethiopian subsidiary for $14 million.
summary: On the last trading day, Indian markets closed lower with the Nifty ending at 22,600, snapping two weeks of gains as crude oil traded near $114. Corporate developments were highlighted by Coforge raising its margin guidance and Kilitch Drugs divesting its Ethiopian arm. Meanwhile, regulatory scrutiny on Gland Pharma and rising commodity bills for Tata Motors framed key stock-specific actions.
